name: Minor Image
description:
Concentration, up to 1 minute.

You create the image of an object, a creature, or another visible phenomenon no larger than 5 ft in any dimension. The image appears at a point within long range. It seems fully real, including appropriate sounds, smells, and temperature, though you can’t create sensory effects that would harm a creature.

Physical interaction reveals the illusion, as objects can pass through it. If a creature spends an action to examine the illusion, roll Insight vs Awareness against the creature. On a loss, the illusion is revealed to that creature: it can see through the image, and the illusion's other sensory qualities become faint to it.

Describe the illusion.
successes:
✨: On a win, the creature takes -1d to any subsequent non-physical attempts to inspect the Illusion.

🌞: On a win, the creature automatically fails any subsequent non-physical attempts to inspect the Illusion. On a loss, the creature checks a Condition, as they begin to doubt the reality of other objects around them.

improvements.name: Programmed Image
improvements.description:
You may spend 1 minute casting this spell as a ritual. If you do, the image does not appear immediately. Instead, define a triggering event. The event must be something that could be observed sensorially from the chosen point.

When the triggering event occurs, the image appears and persists for 1 minute, then goes dormant. 1 minute must pass before the image can be triggered again.

You may define movements and changes to the image - as well as sounds - that will occur over the course of the minute each time the image is triggered.

If you cast the spell in this way, it does not require concentration and it persists until dispelled.

improvements.name: Major Image
improvements.description:
When you cast this spell, you may spend an additional 2 MP. If you do, the image you create may be up to 20 ft in any dimension and you may sustain the effect for up to 10 minutes.

Additionally, while you remain within long range of the illusion, you may spend an action to move it a distance up to your Speed to any other point within long range. As it moves, you can alter its appearance so its behavior remains natural—for example, making a creature appear to walk, or changing its sounds over time, including carrying on a conversation.
